principle: A learner's CEFR-aligned A1 estimate counts a communicative domain as demonstrated only when EVERY objective listed for that domain below carries a real 'demonstrated' checkpoint verdict under the latest-attempt policy. The list is the authored denominator: it names every essential objective that is aligned directly to an A1 descriptor scale in the domain. Non-essential direct objectives are listed under excludedObjectiveIds with the pedagogical reason; nothing is omitted silently. The A1 Capstone samples one representative objective per domain and therefore can contribute evidence but can never complete a domain on its own.

domains.rationale: Facts in a recording, announcements and safety instructions, and dialogues: the three A1 listening activities the Section 3 checkpoint scores. Word recognition is direct at Pre-A1 only and is not listed here.
Messages, notices and short texts: the three A1 reading activities the Section 3 checkpoint scores. Kana and word recognition are direct at Pre-A1 only or supporting, and are not listed here.

excludedObjectiveIds.reason: Short separate phrases only. It is practiced and reported on its own; the estimate does not depend on it.

domains.rationale: Set phrases, self-introduction and simple facts: what a Vietnamese worker needs first in Japan, all checked from recognized words.

excludedObjectiveIds.reason: Discrete labelled fields. It is practiced and reported on its own, and proves less than guided sentences do, so the estimate does not depend on it.

domains.rationale: Personal facts, sentences and a short message: the three guided writing activities the Section 5 checkpoint scores.
Conversation and practical tasks together: an A1 estimate needs both talking with someone and getting something done.
